prompt: Keep a JSlider and a JSpinner showing the same number, clamping every value to the slider's bounds so the spinner model never rejects it. Complete the starter file, then run the tests.
explanation: JSlider and JSpinner both hold a bounded number, but they disagree about what to do with an out-of-range one: BoundedRangeModel clamps quietly while SpinnerNumberModel throws IllegalArgumentException. Clamping once in setValue and then feeding the same clamped number to both keeps them consistent and keeps the exception from ever firing. Reading the step size from the model rather than hard-coding 5 means stepUp stays correct if the model is ever rebuilt with different bounds. JSpinner.getValue returns Object, so casting to Number and calling intValue is the safe way to get an int out of it.
hints: Clamp with two if statements against slider.getMinimum() and slider.getMaximum() before you touch either component.
JSpinner.getValue() returns an Object -- cast it to Number rather than to Integer, then call intValue().
stepUp does not need its own clamping logic: read the step size, then call your own setValue with getValue() plus that step and let setValue do the clamping.
